references.text: Balaam refers back to his earlier reply to Balak's messengers, where he said he could not go beyond the Lord's word, even if Balak gave him his house full of silver and gold.
Reference to when Balak sent his messengers to Balaam for the first time to bring him to curse Israel.
Balak sent yet more and more honorable messengers to Balaam with promises of great honor, which Balaam now refers back to.
Balaam repeats the same principle to Balak personally—that he can only speak what God puts in his mouth.
Balaam emphasizes again that he must say what the Lord puts in his mouth, the same theme as in 24:12.
Balaam reminds Balak that he must do everything the Lord says, a recurring motif throughout the entire story.
